content.text: VerdBoard Documentation

Use this English entry to choose a reading path through the maintained native documents. The Chinese navigation is the primary directory; diagrams explain relationships and mechanisms alongside the same source documents.
Folder workspaces inside projects
A workspace is a real folder, either standalone or embedded in a project. Desktop and the project Web SDK edit the same workspace files through the shared Node host.

Set workspace to a relative directory in .verd.config.json, or pass workspacePath to createProjectWorkspaceService from @sue/verd-board-agent/node. Mount handleRequest on the existing local HTTP server and use createServiceWorkspaceHost with WorkspaceApp. This entry covers local project editing; remote collaboration and static publishing remain outside this stage.

Configuration and attachments remain portable. Personal Web and Desktop sessions are isolated by host. Opening folders preserves Agent instructions; enable or repair authoring tools explicitly in Settings. Project, workspace and repository roots are resolved separately without writing machine-specific paths into project configuration.

Verification follows foundation, domain, rendering, shared-service, product and host boundaries. Unchanged upstream units reuse matching verification evidence; shared business journeys run in production Web, with Desktop and development-runtime contracts covering their differences. Submit packaging once and let the runner collect a terminal summary. See the development guide for commands and policy.
Content reviewed: 2026-11-13, against current repository source, package manifests and the lockfile. Dated acceptance records retain their original scope.

Start with the project documents and follow diagram links for visual explanations. Desktop and local Web open the bundled System introduction in read-only mode. Maintain the native sources in the repository workspace.

Development and validation
Quick Start
Requirements: Node.js >= 22.12.0 and pnpm >= 11.18.0. Root package.json, package manifests and pnpm-lock.yaml define the actual commands and dependency versions.

pnpm install
# Local preview only when explicitly requested
pnpm dev:desktop
# Or preview the Web application
pnpm dev:web
# Check the remote test host before choosing validation scope
pnpm test:remote doctor

On Home, find entries under My workspaces by name or folder, choose Import workspace to open an existing directory, or browse System introduction and Document authoring recommendations. To create a workspace, enter a name, choose the parent folder in the form, and select Create. Click the workspace name to open the My workspaces dropdown over the sidebar navigation. Pinned workspaces appear first. The Workspace page contains All content and Charts with file filters and saved views. Search opens a compact dialog scoped to the current workspace. Cmd/Ctrl+P starts in Title and path and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F starts in All. Content matches show an excerpt and open the matching text or canvas element.
Development and release validation

Fix owners repair defects and run targeted regression tests. Release control validates the complete final snapshot, collects independent failures and blocks packaging whenever a required stage fails or cannot run. Desktop packaging defaults to the isolated test host, reuses this run’s validated build and Agent resources, and retains all four Web/Desktop development/production E2E suites plus real installer checks. Unit and Web tests use bounded parallelism; native desktop tests remain serial within one GUI session. Every release still requires the three business reviews and a substantive system-introduction update.

Use the repository root AGENTS.md to choose content-specific checks or feature-scoped validation on the test Mac. Fixed snapshots include uncommitted changes, jobs survive disconnects, and reports remain bound to their source. Setup and reconnect commands are documented in the development guide under Tailscale 远程开发验收。

Development-machine check:dev and check:ci commands delegate remotely by default. Direct Desktop E2E rejects an unmarked local session before launching Electron; explicit local debugging and CI contexts are documented in the development guide.
Agent and SDK integration
Agent integration and independent content updates

Workspaces expose AGENTS.md, portable project configuration and a shared verd CLI for AI authoring. System introduction and the Document authoring recommendations ship with Desktop and share the product version. In the workspace switcher, choose Open system introduction. An update marker appears inside the corresponding workspace when the bundled content differs from the installed copy. Backups are optional; choosing a backup folder creates a copy in the normal workspace list. See the development and desktop guides for details.

The source baseline is 0.1.0. The standalone Agent uses the shared workspace core. SDK consumers can compose domain plugins and render a read-only canvas. Agent defaults and user recommendations are maintained separately.

Home lists workspaces in Desktop and the local Web editor. Each app restores its workspace selection and tabs. Workspace Overview, Search, All Content, and Pinned files belong to the current workspace. Quick Create and independent file editing are Desktop features. Use Collapse sidebar to the right of Settings at the bottom of the sidebar. Pin or unpin a workspace file from its file menu. Clicking a file from Home or Quick Create returns to its workspace and opens the file.

Choose Start Agent from a page toolbar, the file tree, or the command palette. Every task starts in the current workspace. A file, folder, or selection supplies focus. Codex is the default under Settings → Personal → Agent. Desktop and local Web can run the installed CLI, review proposed native changes, or open a draft in Codex. See the workspace guide for setup.
Workspace prompts and standard Skills

Settings → Prompts edits common workspace instructions and pattern supplements as standard .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md files, with YAML metadata and Markdown bodies. Default patterns and native validation continue to apply. verd context lists workspaceSkills for agents to read on demand; Skill changes invalidate pending plans. File-version conflicts preserve drafts, and bundled workspace updates preserve user Skills and referenced resources.
Independent custom Skills and default Skill viewing

Settings → Custom Skills provides creation, editing and recycling of independently named workspace Skills. Standard SKILL.md files under .agents/skills are discovered automatically. Names are fixed after creation; descriptions and Markdown bodies remain editable, while optional metadata and reference resources are preserved. Custom Skills have no pattern association and agents activate them only when their descriptions match the task.

View default Skill on the Prompts page reads the common authoring Skill, selected pattern Skill and Markdown references. Markdown is the sole source of Agent instructions; executable templates remain native JSON. The viewer offers a read-only model and original Markdown source. Custom Skills provide only the common default entry.
Shared workspace SDK and standalone Agent

The shared @sue/verd-board-workspace package owns native file models, host contracts, sessions, conditional commits, validation and common Git support. Product applications and the standalone Node Agent use the same implementation. Agent API and CLI consumers do not install product app/ui packages; existing product exports remain compatible.

Agent code and content live under packages/agent; the shared workspace core lives under packages/workspace. Product UI source is grouped into canvas, documents, workspace, settings and shared modules. Native system documentation remains in the root workspace folder, and existing application build scripts generate bundled resources directly.
User authoring recommendations provide advice and examples. They are maintained independently from executable Agent defaults and never become default Agent instructions.

Knowledge authoring and reusable content
For slash insertion, reusable paragraphs, templates, content properties, manual versions and folder/ZIP migration, see
Product overview
Document and resource reading
For folding, LaTeX, attachments, PDF/media reading, HTTPS embeds and current limitations, see
Product overview
Portable resources and host capabilities

Native exports with managed resources use verd-canvas-bundle v2 and validate hashes before a single conditional commit. The Desktop application and local Web service both use real filesystem workspaces and provide directory selection, bundled-content updates and Agent tools. The standalone IndexedDB SDK host provides a browser virtual workspace. Source files, resources and saved names retain the same identities across supported hosts.

Regression verification covers unit tests, Web and Desktop development and production builds, real package consumers and fresh Agent resources. Doctor exits 0 when ready and 1 when unready without initializing the project.

Ordinary resources appear at their real paths and open in a read-only preview or the system application (download on Web). Project data, assets, history and cache live under the excluded .verdscrolls/ directory. Every diagram is an independent source file, shown once in the directory tree; canvases share it through stable references. Existing resource stores migrate without rewriting attachment addresses.
Git versions

Workspace versions use the enclosing Git repository. Standalone workspaces can own a repository; project document directories inherit their parent repository, including linked worktrees. Explicit commits, history reads and restores stay inside the content directory. Saving creates no automatic commits or recovery checkpoints.

Standalone filesystem workspaces retain system Git credentials and manual remote synchronization. Project document directories leave repository settings, branches, synchronization and history rewriting to external Git tools. Ordinary permanent trash deletion preserves committed history; standalone repositories expose separate advanced history cleanup. Legacy snapshots remain readable and restorable.

File and directory menus provide Version history with explicit creation, preview and restore. Workspace settings → Version management contains workspace history and storage configuration. Git is the current adapter behind a provider-independent service. Directory identity follows moves and renames from its first identified version; restore targets its current location.
Local Web service

Run pnpm dev:web to start the Web UI and local service at http://localhost:7200. Build with pnpm build:web and serve the production UI and API with pnpm start:web. The Web application uses filesystem workspaces and supports directory selection, Git remote sync, shared Agent tools and bundled-content updates. Development, production and tests use separate data directories.

Use Settings → Data and maintenance → Migrate browser data to back up and import existing IndexedDB workspaces, including files, resources, Skills, sessions, trash and Git history. After a successful validated import, the source IndexedDB records are cleared and the complete backup is retained. Failed imports and changed source records are kept. Detection requires the original browser origin; importing a backup file does not clear current browser data.
Quick Create and desktop file associations

Desktop opens workspaces in a single main window. To return to it while an independent window is open, use the tray, the macOS Dock, or Window → Show Main Window. Opening a diagram from a known workspace switches to that workspace and opens the diagram as a tab.

Choose Quick Create below Home to browse files in the VerdBoard user data directory’s quick-edit/ folder. The same page lists up to 20 independent files recently opened from other folders. Desktop keeps these files at their existing locations. Use Rename in the list or the file window to change the filename while keeping its extension. Move to Trash asks for confirmation. Remove from Recent clears the entry and keeps the file. Interactive Desktop development uses the repository’s Git-ignored tmp/verdboard/quick-edit/ folder.

Right-click the desktop tray icon to create a file, create a whiteboard, mind map, flowchart, architecture diagram, UML class diagram, or UML sequence diagram, create a workspace, reopen VerdScrolls, or quit. With an available tray, closing the last window keeps the app running. Quitting uses the usual save confirmation.

Use File → Open File or ⌘O on macOS and Ctrl+O on Windows and Linux. Use the letter O for opening and the digit 0 for resetting page zoom. The file picker supports .md, .markdown, .verd, and legacy .verd.json. The installed desktop app can also open Markdown and .verd files from the system file manager.
